title: The Retadup worm revives from old USB drives to download CoffeeLoader | Kaspersky official blog
description: The Retadup worm, originally widespread in 2017 and dismantled in 2019, has resurfaced through infected old USB drives and offline computers. The worm spreads by copying itself to connected flash drives and external disks as hidden files and shortcuts. After French law enforcement took down the botnet in 2019 by seizing its C2 servers and issuing self-destruct commands, the worm was thought eradicated from online systems. However, in 2024, attackers re-registered Retadup's old C2 domain names, reactivating the botnet for infected offline systems or USB drives. The worm now downloads the more advanced CoffeeLoader malware, which uses sophisticated evasion techniques and can download further malware such as infostealers or ransomware. Retadup infection attempts have been detected primarily in Peru, Angola, and Russia. Users are advised to disable autorun, scan old drives before use, and maintain updated security software.
